preamble: In Japanese /z/ before /i/ and in /zj/ yōon syllables is realized as the alveolo-palatal affricate [dʑ] varying with the fricative [ʑ]. The affricate is more frequent after a pause or a moraic consonant and in slower speech, the fricative in faster speech. Most dialects have also merged original /zi, zj/ with /di, dj/ in this phone (the yotsugana merger), while Tosa keeps /zi/ and /di/ apart. Historically [dʑ] was the realization of /d/ before /i/, and /z/ came to share it through this merger.

examples.note: /z/ before /i/ is palatalized and realized as [dʑ ~ ʑ].
Intervocalic /zi/ shows the same [dʑ ~ ʑ] variation.

context: Japanese /zj/ and /z/ before /i/; [dʑ] favoured after a pause or moraic consonant and in slow speech, [ʑ] in faster speech
